clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 621-2076 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10570.txt, 19 FR 6687): signed 1954-10-16; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between The Pullman Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). The held National Mediation Board report for this board (Emergency Board No. 107; jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10570_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10570_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_f1cbeae2b3.txt) bears the cover date NOVEMBER 20, 1954 (date line at offsets 1190-1207 of that held text), so the board's reporting command was functionally spent on 1954-11-20. The report states that by stipulation of the parties the time for making the report was extended to November 26, 1954 (report text offsets 2848-2990); its letter of transmittal is also dated November 20, 1954. The extension approvals are not held instruments and bear only on the report deadline. The thirty-day standstill that the order recites ran, by its own terms, for thirty days after the report, that is to 1954-12-20 (computed, not stated in a held source); that period also ended long before 1986. Both dates are spent facts, not ends. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10570 appears in the table at offset 10470 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.

research_rationale:
EO 10570 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1954-11-20 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.
